summary: 116/23 eye-subject gaze construction is already quoted; index it under the gaze idiom rather than literal Detransitive sense 1.
rationale: The paired eye subjects and m-person complements express not looking away; no physical eye severing occurs. The new idiom reuses this evidence without counting another box example.

summary: Restore the first-person possessive suffix
rationale: The corpus reads mam morayḏi, with the first-person ending -i. The current -e gives third-person possession, contradicting qṭəʕlux-li and my relatives. This changes the person, not a spelling convention.

summary: Restore the conditional opening
rationale: The excerpt starts iḏa d- (if), and ʕaqəl diḏi identifies the first-person subject. The current German has no subject and no conditional conjunction before so werde ich. The corpus translation repeats the incomplete wording, so the repair rests on the supplied Turoyo, not on that German fragment.

summary: Restore the reflexive condition of the wager
rationale: The Turoyo məġbən is the person becoming angry, not a person angering a female object. The cited wager expressly says Dem, welcher sich ärgert. Substituting sie reverses the condition of punishment.

summary: Translate tre as two months
rationale: The supplied Turoyo says me tre yarḥe, two months. Three is tloṯo, also attested in this entry in tloṯo=qarʕe. The English numeral is inconsistent with the example.

summary: 58/208 torn rag belongs to literal tearing, not cessation of blood flow.
rationale: qappāl qṭiʕo is parallel to torn nylon and clothes; Detransitive sense 2 denotes cessation.

summary: File the torn rag under detransitive sense 1
rationale: Qappāl qṭiʕo is a torn rag, as the edition confirms with zerrissenen ... Lumpen. Detransitive sense 1 is abgerissen werden / zerreissen; sense 2 is blood ceasing to flow and does not fit cloth.

data.translation: Die Frau macht sich auf, wie die Armen Leute, und kommt zu dem Hause des Mädchens." Um Gottes willen, gib mir Unterkunft! Meine Freunde sind fortgegangen und ich bin ganz verlassen", und was der gleichen Reden mehr sind.

data.turoyo: Mqaṭʕiwo i qarʕo, masala gdəmmina hawxa xi paṭata d..., qulfiwo i qarʕo ʕawwəl naqqa, mqaṭʕiwola hawxa falqe, hno, küp, e, mən kəmmitunne? Hawxa, [ST: mrabʕe?] e, mrabʕe ... e, mrabʕe w xəd ṣanṭin raqiqe, w hani, haṯe i qarʕo yo.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 2.3/4)

data.turoyo: Aq qarʕanək ḥulmiwo w huwewulle bəzarʕo šafiro, rabo b gawayye, qarʕe rabe, bu saṯwo hanək stene b ḥašwo u mede, d sayminawo b baṣro hano, hanək ste qulfinawull, mqaṭʕinawulle, qulfinawo u lebaṯṯe ste hawxa d lowe ..., əmmiwo hawxa rakixo yo, latyo basimo.
data.translation: Diese Kürbisse wurden dick und hatten schöne große Kerne im Inneren. Es waren große Kürbisse, im Winter bereiteten wir auch sie mit Füllung zu, Füllung mit Fleisch. Die Kürbisse schälten wir, schnitten sie in Stücke, entfernten das Innere, damit es nicht .... man sagte, es ist zu weich, es schmeckt nicht.

rationale: Adds suffixed first-person II Infectum-wa for comparison with the zero-marked patient.

data.translation: Man hackte die Zwiebeln ganz fein und mischte das Hackfleisch, das gehackte, das feingehackte Fleisch darunter. Das Fleisch musste mehr sein als die Zwiebeln.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum example of existing relationship-separation sense 3.

summary: example for sense 1b in Part. Pass. (70/206)

data.turoyo: Komər mhalaxxe me ṣafrayto w hul ʕaṣriye. Yawme du qayṭo yo w ḥemo yo, ṣahən. Am mayaṯṯe xaliṣi, darbo maqṭuʕ yo. Lo walayat, lo mede layt bu darbo.
data.translation: Sie ritten vom Morgen bis zum Abend. Es war ein heißer Sommertag, sie wurden Durstig. Das Wasser ging ihnen aus, und der Weg war abgelegen; keine Städte und nichts war auf dem Wege.

rationale: Best contextual evidence for remote/isolated maqṭuʕ; absence of settlements is explicit.

summary: example for sense 4 in Preterit-wa (82/30)

data.turoyo: Hani qṭiʕiwa me gaban, me šawʕo babe, qṭiʕi as səsyani aḥ ḥewore w semoqe. Adyawma səsto me diḏi hawila, muhro balak."
data.translation: Diese, die weiß-roten Pferde, waren bei uns vor sieben Vätern ausgestorben. Heute hat eine meiner Stuten ein scheckiges Fohlen geworfen."

rationale: Introduces Detransitive sense 4 in Preterit-wa; the shared sentence also contains token 137.

summary: example for sense 4 in Preterit-wa (82/68)

data.turoyo: Omər məlleli: "Kule u ṭaršano diḏi yo. Bas mede ḥa, d komabxeli, me šawʕo babe, kəmmənne annaqla hənne raxša balak, qṭiʕiwa as səsye balak me gaban.
data.translation: Er sprach zu mir: All dies Vieh gehört mir; aber es gibt etwas, das mich Weinen läßt: vor sieben Vätern waren die scheckigen Pferde - diese Leutenennen sie "rachscha bäläk" - bei uns ausgestorben.

rationale: Second independent verse supports extinction of the horse line.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (94/393)

data.turoyo: Hawxa gsoyəm ḥa mənne, hul d məqṭəʕ ḥəs diḏe. Me d qṭiʕ ḥəs diḏe, edi gdoṯe ḥreno l dukṯe, gbode d soyəm u ḥəmgeliyo.
data.translation: So macht es ersteiner, bis ihm der Atem ausgeht, dann tritt ein anderer an seine Stelle und fängt mit dem Gebrumme an.

rationale: Adds ḥəs-subject cessation to Detransitive Infectum sense 2; same passage contains completed token 145.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (94/393)

data.turoyo: Hawxa gsoyəm ḥa mənne, hul d məqṭəʕ ḥəs diḏe. Me d qṭiʕ ḥəs diḏe, edi gdoṯe ḥreno l dukṯe, gbode d soyəm u ḥəmgeliyo.
data.translation: So macht es ersteiner, bis ihm der Atem ausgeht, dann tritt ein anderer an seine Stelle und fängt mit dem Gebrumme an.

rationale: Adds completed voice cessation to Detransitive Preterit sense 2.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (94/394)

data.turoyo: Haxa maxlaṣṣe, maṭən li ḥəlle, heš d lo qṭiʕ u nafasaṯṯe, maxlaṣṣe, yaʕni mqayzanne.
data.translation: Wenn sie es fertigbringen, die Freistatt zu erreichen, ohne daß ihnen der Atem ausgeht, so haben sie gewonnen.

rationale: Adds breath as a further cessation subject in Detransitive Preterit sense 2.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/61)

data.turoyo: Mənayye lə kuḏʕi, kmaḥtile b šəriṭo, naqlat kməqṭəʕ u šəriṭo w kəzze u taʕab dəṯṯe bi hawa.
data.translation: Einige kennen sich nicht aus, sie hängen sie an eine Schnur, und manchmal reißt dann die Schnur und ihre ganze Mühe war umsonst.

rationale: Fills the fifth Detransitive Infectum sense-1 slot with spontaneous string breakage.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/13)

data.turoyo: Šqəlle u+zʕuro mənne. Koḥayri, mətwile, lo admo, lo naparušk̇e, lo aǧ+ǧulayḏe qṭiʕi, lo mede, xud ruḥe.
data.translation: They took the boy away from them. They take a look, they sit him up, neither blood, nor a scratch, nor his clothes torn, nor anything at all, like himself (i.e., like he was before).

rationale: Fills the thin Detransitive Preterit D1 cell with finite-shaped qṭiʕi; contrast with verse 15 is retained as a question.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (108/8)

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm, qrallale lu waziro, aṯi: “Ha, u šulṭonayḏi, mənyaṯi? Mə kəmmat?” Omər: “Qum, izux, qṭaʕ i šariʕa di kurfo, ono, laybi qoṭaʕno i šariʕa di kurfo. Ono buxa, i salṭanayḏi ste ṭruyo elux w i šariʕa di kurfo, laybi qoṭaʕna.”
data.translation: Man rief den Wesir herbei; er kam. - Nun, mein Sultan, was ist denn geschehen? Was hast du zu sagen? - Mach dich auf und schlichte den Rechtshandel der Schlange, ich kann ihn nicht schlichten. Meine Sultansherrschaft selbst soll dir überlassen sein; ich kann den Rechtshandel der Schlange nicht entscheiden. -

rationale: Adds the contracted qoṭaʕna form under existing legal sense 2; unresolved segmentation is flagged.

summary: example for sense 11 in Infectum (108/27)

data.turoyo: Hala ono me lawġul lo nofaqwayno, aydarbo qəṭʕat u xer me lawġul diḏi?
data.translation: Ich pflegte doch nie auszugehen; wie kannst die guten werke außerhalb meines Hauses einstellen?

rationale: Adds charity withholding as an extension of I.11.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (108/46)

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm azzən su malla, lu malla qṭəʕle i šariʕatte, məlle: “Fəlgayye elux ne, faqir, w fəlgayye lu təǧǧar ne.”
data.translation: Sie gingen zum Molla. Der entschied: Die Hälfte gehört dir, dem Armen, und die Hälfte dem Kaufmann. -

rationale: Fills Preterit sense 2 with explicit legal adjudication.

summary: example for sense 11 in Preterit (112/13)

data.turoyo: Kul yawmo ḥozewayni ṣaydo, rowaḥwa lebi, adyawma qṭəʕlux u naṣib diḏi, ḥatta disa d ak kulayḏi daʕiri, xəd meqəm.
data.translation: Jeden Tag habe ich Wildpret gefunden, und es wurde mir wohl ums Herz; heute aber hast du mir meinen Anteil vorenthalten, so daß mein Kummer wiedergekommen ist, wie zuvor.

rationale: Adds withholding an allotted share to I.11.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (112/49)

data.turoyo: Komər qrele l Kalaš ʕAli, lu abro, d kətwe mi barriye, d ḥzewayle. Məlle: “Ya abri, halux, ʕbar li odaṯe, d siməlli adyawma, laḥ ḥadode d babux, mə ʕaqəl diḏux gqoṭəʕ mena?”
data.translation: Dann rief er Kalasch Ali, den Sohn aus der Steppe, den er gefunden hatte, und sprach: Mein Sohn! Komm, geh in dieses Zimmer hinein, das ich heute von den Schmieden deines Vaters habe machen lassen. Was hältst du davon? -

rationale: Brings the confidence Infectum cell to five; m-stimulus matches the existing ability construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/83)

data.turoyo: I gwetaṯe kmašəġila, bəṯr məd hawyo, w kəmqaṭʕila, kəmmalḥila,
data.translation: Nachdem dieser Käse fertig ist, waschen sie ihn, schneiden ihn in Stücke und salzen ihn.

rationale: Fills II Infectum sense 1 with an independently understandable cheese-preparation clause.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Lahdo The ḥalile/6)

data.turoyo: ḥzo b ḥzo gәmqaṭʕinala gsayminala arbʕo falqe, әšto, aydarbo d hawi.
data.translation: One by one we slice them and make them four pieces, six, or however they become.

rationale: Fills the fifth II Infectum slot with explicit cutting into pieces; no culinary subsense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 38/61)

data.turoyo: Mqaṭʕole bam muwas, maḥtole ʕal i nuro. Maṭfela i nuro, səmola faḥmo bu samo.
data.translation: dann zerschnitt er sie mit einem scharfen Messer in kleine Stücke und legte diese auf's Feuer. Aber das Feuer erlosch und ward zu Kola gemacht durch das Gift.

rationale: Fills II Preterit with feminine object indexing; snake is recoverable from the source context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/57)

data.turoyo: kəmqaṭʕile, ksaymile falqe, heš huwe b gawe du səfoqo, w kmaqləbile ʕal dukṯo mede d nəšfo, ǧule aw taxtayat naḏ̣ife,
data.translation: <...> schneiden sie die ḥărire in Stücke, während sie noch auf dem Teller liegt, und legen sie dann irgendwohin, wo sie trocknen kann, auf Stoff oder auf saubere Bretter.

rationale: Fills II Infectum at five examples together with cheese and ḥawdal; dish context keeps the patient clear.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 1.8/151)

data.turoyo: <...> əno w hat lu zabno qṭəʕlelan mə ḥḏoḏe. <...>
data.translation: <...> time has not cut me and you off from one another. <...>

rationale: Fifth Preterit I.1 example; time is the causer of interpersonal separation already included in I.1.

summary: example for sense 3b in Preterit (Jan 1.8/211)

data.turoyo: Qayəm azzano uno w xale Ḥabbo qamayto layo d be Maxxule w ḥərlan aʕla, lə qṭəʕle ʕaqəl diḏan mena. <...>
data.translation: Then Aunt Habbo and I went first to the Maxxule woman and looked at her; our mind did not settle on her. <...>

rationale: First Preterit example of the new preference subsense 3b.

summary: example for sense 3b in Infectum (Jan 1.8/212)

data.turoyo: <...> Ḥzay ayna d qoṭəʕ ʕaqəl diḏox mena, gəd ṭəlbinala.
data.translation: <...> See whichever your mind settles on, and we will ask for her. <...>

rationale: First Infectum 3b; explicit spouse choice and m-stimulus.

summary: example for sense 3b in Preterit (Jan 1.8/227)

data.turoyo: <...> Kan qṭəʕlox ʕaqəl diḏox mena, gəd saymina šuġlox w dlo stene, bəṯr d lə saymət gazəne meni. <...>
data.translation: <...> If you have made up your mind about her, we will arrange your affair, and otherwise too, provided you do not make trouble for me. <...>

rationale: Adds the unusual personal l-agent with ʕaqəl in the preference construction; do not silently replace -lox.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.16/656)

data.turoyo: <...> Əzzənwo l tamo qəṭʕiwo kefe, hani daq qatore w kətwo i šeno d Maḥṣaraṯa b Məḏyaḏ qəṭʕiwo. <...>
data.translation: <...> They went there and cut stones, those of the Qatore, and there was the rock of Mahsarata in Midyat, where they cut stone. <...>

rationale: Fourth I.1 Infectum-wa example; quarrying context contrasts with timber cutting.

summary: example for sense 11 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.16/688)

data.turoyo: <...> hul ṣafro i nuro lə qəṭʕiwola, u atuno hul d yoqəḏ kayiso. <...>
data.translation: <...> they would not cut off the fire, so that the kiln would burn properly. <...>

rationale: Introduces Infectum-wa for round-one I.11: maintaining the firing process rather than severing a physical object.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (Jan 2.1/13)

data.turoyo: <...> W a kṯowe w a frose, d kətle bi beṯ-arkayḏa, dayəm umarwoli: "Ǧan, tamo ne! Qṭəʕno mənayye!" <...>
data.translation: <...> And the books and publications that he has in its library—he would always tell me, 'Jan, they are there! I am cut off from them!' <...>

rationale: Fourth Detransitive Preterit 3 example; separation from possessions and unusual ə-vocalism are retained explicitly.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 2.5/1187)

data.turoyo: <...> taq w taq, taq w taq, w ġurm, ġurm w u ḥəs lə kməqṭəʕ m ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: <...> bang and bang, bang and bang, and boom, boom; the sound does not cease.

rationale: Adds repeated sound plus reciprocal complement to the still-thin Detransitive Infectum 2 cell.

summary: example for sense 3c in Infectum (Jan 2.7/1851)

data.turoyo: <...> bas lə kqoṭəʕ ʕaqəl diḏi, d kətne ahəl, pəsmam. Latne pəsmam. <...>
data.translation: <...> but my mind does not accept that they are relatives, cousins. They are not cousins. <...>

rationale: First 3c Infectum example; explicit rejection of a kinship proposition.

summary: example for sense 12 in Preterit (Jan 2.10/2316)

data.turoyo: <...> Qṭəʕle qumayye omər: "Əno ʕal i šariʕa du Abuna w lo ʕal i šariʕaṯxu."
data.translation: <...> He cut in before them and says: "I follow Abuna's religious law and not your religious law."

rationale: Only attestation of new conversational sense 12; preserves corrective speech as evidence.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 2.12/2970)

data.turoyo: <...> Fekiye kətwo, mab baḏənǧan səmoqani, kətwolle musəm, tre yarḥe-tloṯo, bu qayṭo w bəṯər məqṭəʕiwo. Uʕdo haw fayəš kməqṭoʕi abadan. <...>
data.translation: <...> There was fruit, those tomatoes. They had their season, two months or three, in summer, and afterwards they used to run out. Now they no longer run out at all. <...>

rationale: Adds the aspectual contrast to Detransitive Infectum 2; paired past/present account makes availability explicit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.12/3157)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Warox yabo aḥna, aḥna lə mzabanlan! Ḥaram aʕlayna! Qəṭʕinawo, yaʕni məlenawo lagane.
data.translation: Father Brahim: Come now, my boy, we, we did not sell it! Shame on us! We cut it, that is, we filled basins.

rationale: Fifth literal I.1 Infectum-wa example, retaining unusual first-person form and honey-harvesting context.

summary: example for sense 4 in Preterit (Jan 2.20/3800)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Ooooooo Alo ṭurelox! Hul meqəm bə ḥṣar əšne aq qalme b Məḏyaḏ wayye. Meqəm 10-15 əšne kətwo. Hani 20 əšne d qṭiʕi bad darmonani d mawfaqla li ḥkume.
data.translation: Father Brahim: Ooooooo, may God spare you! Until ten years ago there were lice in Midyat. Ten to fifteen years ago there were. It is twenty years since they disappeared, with those chemicals that the government brought out.

rationale: First Detransitive Preterit 4 example after round-one extinction sense; government chemicals give an explicit causal adjunct.

summary: example for sense 3c in Infectum (Jan 2.26/4422)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni u mede d aḥna baḥ ḥayayḏan ḥzelan, lə kqoṭəʕ ʕaqəl diḏi, ǧil ḥreno, doro ḥreno, ḥzalle u mede d ḥzelan.
data.translation: That is, what we saw in our lives, my mind cannot conceive that another generation, another age, should have seen what we saw.

rationale: Second 3c Infectum example; clausal content contrasts with the m-marked preference frame.

summary: example for sense 3 in Part. Pass. (Jan 3.11/116)

data.turoyo: <...> An noše, d azzən lu ḥtiyat, fayiši əšne qṭiʕe man nošaṯṯe, mʕaḏbi bu ʕwodo. Daʕiri lab bote.
data.translation: <...> The men who went into reserve service remained for years cut off from their families, suffering through labour. They returned to their homes.

rationale: First Part. Pass. for round-one relational sense 3; plural -e contrasts with finite -i.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (Jan 3.47/1299)

data.turoyo: <...> Ono naʕəmto, maṯ w an naʕimayḏe azzən l Suriya w hedi qṭiʕo i ʕalaqayḏi mənne, lo kəḏʕono.
data.translation: <...> I was little when he died, and his children went to Syria, and then my connection with them was cut off; I do not know.

rationale: Fifth Detransitive Preterit 3 example; the relationship itself is the feminine subject.

summary: Restore keinen in the negative object
rationale: The indefinite human object is masculine accusative keinen. The corpus has ließ keinen gehen und kommen, corresponding to negative noše.

summary: Correct the case after sich verlieben in
rationale: Sich in jemanden verlieben takes accusative, so dir must be dich.

summary: Sense 2: revise the gloss
after: zu fliessen aufhören, stocken (Blutkreislauf); auch: aufhören (Stimme, Atem, Besucherverkehr);
rationale: Blood, ḥəs, nafas and dawse occur as subjects of cessation; this broadens the established meaning without creating parallel senses for each subject.

summary: Sense 3: revise the gloss
after: sich trennen, den Verkehr miteinander abbrechen (mit m-);
rationale: 42/2 and 63/187,200 establish reciprocal separation and ending a relationship; replaces the tentative English gloss.

summary: New idiom: u sayfo qoṭəʕ 'die Macht durchsetzen, Gewalt ausüben' (vorläufig)

data.headword: u sayfo qoṭəʕ 'die Macht durchsetzen, Gewalt ausüben' (vorläufig)
data.turoyo: Suč, lək+kowe, dəmmina, u+sayfaṯṯe qoṭaʕwa, biḏáyyewe, be+Ḥaǧo ŭ hawxa, ŭ aḥ+ḥawronaṯṯe, az+zabnanək.
data.translation: It was a crime, it wouldn’t happen, let’s say, the gloves would come off (lit. ‘their sword would cut’), it was under their control (lit. ‘hand’), the family of Hajo and so on, and their friends, those times.

rationale: Single sword-subject figurative construction; record as a tentative idiom, with the literal-violence alternative questioned.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ tawbe 'ein Reugelübde ablegen, Buße tun'

data.headword: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ tawbe 'ein Reugelübde ablegen, Buße tun'
data.turoyo: Lázəmyo dəzzúx qəm ʕito daṣ+ṣuroye, quṭʕat tawbe.
data.translation: It is necessary for you to go to a Christian church and make (lit. ‘cut’) penance.

rationale: Light verb with tawbe; one clear collocation, rite details remain open.

summary: New idiom: iḏo qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ m- 'sich von j-m lösen, von j-m lassen' (Detrans.)

data.headword: iḏo qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ m- 'sich von j-m lösen, von j-m lassen' (Detrans.)
data.turoyo: Ummo: "Zox sum bazar w itox lu bayto, arǧaʕ kli aṯtox." Omər: "Lə kməqṭoʕo iḏi menəx."
data.translation: Da sagte sie ihm: »Geh hin, treibe Handel; wenn du nach Hause zurückkommst, bin ich ja wieder deine Frau«. Er aber erwiderte: »Ich kann mich nicht von dir trennen«.

rationale: Merge hand-subject proposals from PrS 4/14,37/23,95/221,96/190 into one idiom; emotional attachment and bodily handling are context variants.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ xabro 'ein Wort vergessen, fallenlassen' (vorläufig)

data.turoyo: Lo qṭəʕle abre du malko u xabro d məllele lu Bani Sabʕa.
data.translation: der Königssohn aber vergass das Wort, welches der Löwenkönig gesprochen hatte, nicht.

rationale: Negated utterance-object construction is distinct from literal cutting; precise force remains uncertain.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ goman m- 'die Hoffnung aufgeben' (Variante zu amal/heviye)

data.headword: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ goman m- 'die Hoffnung aufgeben' (Variante zu amal/heviye)
data.turoyo: qṭəʕwayli u goman minux.
data.translation: Ich hatte die Hoffnung auf dich aufgegeben.

rationale: Adds goman as a noun variant of the existing hope idiom, without a new numbered sense.

summary: New idiom: kazabat (d lebo) qṭiʕi 'vor Schrecken erstarren' (Detrans.; Variante zu hnavat)

data.headword: kazabat (d lebo) qṭiʕi 'vor Schrecken erstarren' (Detrans.; Variante zu hnavat)
data.turoyo: ak kazabataṯṯe qṭiʕi.
data.translation: Da waren sie starr vor Schrecken

rationale: Repeated vital-organ subject variant of the existing fear idiom.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ wariḏe d lebo 'j-n in Angst versetzen, das Herz zerreißen'

data.headword: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ wariḏe d lebo 'j-n in Angst versetzen, das Herz zerreißen'
data.turoyo: Qṭəʕle aw warīḏe d lebi, maz zuḥṯayḏe hawxa komaḏ̣aʕfono”.
data.translation: Er hat mir das Herzählen zerschnitten, aus Angst vor ihm magere ich so ab."

rationale: Single metaphorical heart-veins collocation; no actual severing is asserted.

summary: New idiom: ṣabr qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ 'die Geduld verlieren, den Mut verlieren' (Detrans.; vorläufig)

data.headword: ṣabr qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ 'die Geduld verlieren, den Mut verlieren' (Detrans.; vorläufig)
data.turoyo: Tamo u ṣabrayḏi qṭiʕ w məlli: "Haw kətlan əmkaniye d qodanno ḥozeno u dawlatraysi.
data.translation: Da riß mir die Geduld und ich dachte: Es wird nicht möglich sein, den Staatspräsidenten zu sehen.

rationale: Single possessed abstract-subject idiom; patience versus hope remains a question.

summary: New idiom: lebo qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ 'den Mut verlieren, vor Schrecken erstarren' (Detrans.)

data.headword: lebo qṭiʕ/məqṭəʕ 'den Mut verlieren, vor Schrecken erstarren' (Detrans.)
data.turoyo: Annaqla hiye lebe qṭəʕwa.
data.translation: Ali sein Mut war ihm damals1 entfallen;

rationale: Group heart-subject proposals at 73/418 and 87/85; do not split lost courage and fright into numbered senses.

summary: New idiom: qaṭəʕ ṭariq/ṭarəq 'Wegelagerer' (entlehnte Personenbezeichnung)

data.turoyo: Zlam qaṭəʕ ṭariq yo.
data.translation: Er war ein Wegelagerer.

rationale: Borrowed road-cutter phrase is placed in Idiomatic phrases; it does not establish productive Turoyo Part act.

summary: New idiom: ḥaye qṭiʕi m-arʕo 'das Leben verlieren' (Detrans.)

data.turoyo: Əmmi, qrelale l Ḥasane Aliki, məlla: “Ya Ḥasane Aliki, u rawixawhoke, d moṭelux, he žnuka qṭiʕi aḥ ḥayyayḏux mi arʕo, gqoṭelux.”
data.translation: Sie rief Ḥasan Aliki zu: O Ḥasan Aliki, wenn der Reiter dort dich erreicht, so ist es wiederum um dein Leben geschehen; er wird dich töten. -

rationale: One life-subject figurative collocation with an explicit following killing clause; keep out of the literal D1 cell.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ naqdo 'das Brautgeld festsetzen'

data.turoyo: Komər tamo lu ḥakəm nšəqle iḏe du šex. W ṭlibole w qṭəʕʕe u naqdayḏa, ʕaṣro alfo.
data.translation: Da küßte der Fürst die Hand des Scheichs. Er verlobte das Mädchen, und sie setzten das Brautgeld auf zehntausend fest. -

rationale: Best compact example among three brideprice agreements; one idiom rather than a new numbered monetary sense.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ iḏoṯo m-ḥḏoḏe 'ein Paar voneinander trennen'

data.headword: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ iḏoṯo m-ḥḏoḏe 'ein Paar voneinander trennen'
data.turoyo: Komər məlla: “Ba dele pušte! I masalaṯi, d mamṭyolax b qarʕi w d simolax w d qṭəʕlax iḏi w du rḥimo d lebe d abre d ʕammi m ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: Sif sprach: du Hündin, du hure! Was du mir da auf den Hals gebracht und angestellt hast! du hast meine Hand und die des geliebten meines Herzens, meines Vetters, voneinander getrennt!

rationale: Active hand-separation counterpart of the batch-1 Detransitive hand-attachment construction.

summary: New idiom: wariḏo d lebo qṭiʕ 'vor Schock verzweifeln, erschrecken' (Detrans.; vorläufig)

data.headword: wariḏo d lebo qṭiʕ 'vor Schock verzweifeln, erschrecken' (Detrans.; vorläufig)
data.turoyo: Koməq qṭiʕ u wariḏo d lebi, məlli: "Gidi zoxu bəṯre du taxtur!"
data.translation: Da zerriß mir die Herzader, ich sagte: Geht und holt den Doktor!

rationale: Single heart-vein subject variant of the active vein-cutting image; no unrestricted new emotional sense.

summary: New idiom: zəravat qṭiʕi 'einen Schrecken bekommen' (Detrans.; Variante zu hnavat/kazabat)

data.headword: zəravat qṭiʕi 'einen Schrecken bekommen' (Detrans.; Variante zu hnavat/kazabat)
data.turoyo: Qṭiʕi az zəravat dəṯṯe w kulle maʕlalle ab bayraqe d Usuf Paša
data.translation: Sie bekamen einen Gewaltigen schrecken und erhoben alle die Fahnen von Jusuf Pascha.

rationale: Sinew-subject variant of the established fear idiom; separate lexical noun indexing.

summary: New idiom: ʕayno məqṭəʕ m- 'den Blick von j-m wenden' (Detrans.)

data.headword: ʕayno məqṭəʕ m- 'den Blick von j-m wenden' (Detrans.)
data.turoyo: koḥozeno, i kurfayḏi, ʕayna lo koməqṭoʕo mini w ono ste, ʕayni lə kməqṭoʕo mina.
data.translation: Da sehe ich, daß die Schlange den Blick nicht von mir wendet, und auch ich wende den Blick nicht von ihr,

rationale: Indexes the already quoted paired gaze expression under Idiomatic phrases, with an explicit structure correction.

summary: New idiom: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ ʕalaqa m- 'die Verbindung zu j-m/einem Ort abbrechen'

data.headword: qṭəʕle/qoṭəʕ ʕalaqa m- 'die Verbindung zu j-m/einem Ort abbrechen'
data.turoyo: <...> Aḥuno əno qṭəʕli i ʕalaqayḏi m Səʕərt, hani tarte šne, l Səʕərt lə kəzzino w lə kəzzino l Səʕərt <...>
data.translation: <...> Brother, I cut off my connection with Siirt. For these two years I haven't been going to Siirt, and I haven't been going to Siirt. <...>

rationale: Two texts attest the abstract relationship object; lookup search found no ʕalaqa collocation. Keep the noun construction in Idiomatic phrases rather than duplicate sense 10.

summary: The routine_counts are additional, unexpanded attestations, not missing decisions. They corroborate the high frequency of literal cutting (170 Infectum, 144 Preterit) and the smaller legal, reflexive and Detransitive cells; counted-only tokens receive no decision lines.

All 150 full occurrences were checked in order against their Turoyo and edition translation. Original example wording is retained. Same-source repeated tokens have separate decisions; a shared context is printed only once.

Experiencers are often possessors of the grammatical subject: ʕaqəl for confidence, iḏo for attachment, hnavat/kazabat/lebo for fright. The German or English personal subject must not be projected back into Turoyo syntax.

Detransitive includes spontaneous breakage (string/yarn), externally caused mutilation, reciprocal separation, cessation of flow or activity, and emotional constructions. A single passive interpretation cannot cover these.

II culinary cutting is covered by existing sense 1. Infectum-wa is habitual with dayəm and recipes; bare Infectum also occurs within a past account. Active ko-Preterit reports a completed act currently open to inspection.

qṭilux (57/148) is retained provisionally as a contracted head-cutting form; qoṭəḥ and reduced qṭaʕ compounds are not normalized. The occupational qaṭoʕe and borrowed qaṭəʕ ṭariq are indexed with explicit limits on verbal status.

New idiom searches used glossary_lookup search for tawbe, hand phrases, lebe qṭ, sayfaṯṯe, qaṭəʕ, ṣabr, warīḏ, kazab and goman; twb confirms repentance-vow vocabulary but contains no qṭʕ tawbe collocation. Already listed hope, hnavat and interception phrases are not new senses.

PrS 17/63 and PrS 68/64 repeat existing passages quoted under older page/line references (prs 41/29, 194/37). Do not add them as independent examples or silently rewrite references. 52/156 in the existing first Preterit example differs from the supplied verse; retain for editorial source collation.

Batch 2 continues all batch-1 changes cumulatively and preserves its sense labels. The previous entry.json, entry.md and all 168 decisions were read and checked before continuing; this file adds 17 occurrence decisions and new proposal-group decisions only.

Brideprice naqdo is a negotiated amount in three verses; keep the light-verb collocation in Idiomatic phrases, distinct from already numbered marriage solemnization and legal adjudication. Hand separation gains an active counterpart to the existing Detransitive attachment idiom.

The 116/23 gaze pair is already in the baseline. It is reindexed as an idiom, not duplicated as two new Infectum examples. koqṭiʕ mu xel supplies a new Detransitive ko-Preterit box for separation from a group.
Permitted lookup searches found no qṭʕ naqdo, wariḏo or zəravat collocation. The existing qṭʕ 2 eye example concerns visual extent, not ʕayno + m-person disengagement.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
The literary collection preserves conversational syntax and specialist quarry/kiln terminology; this evidence does not warrant attributing every form to a uniformly learned written register.

ʕaqəl is usually the possessed grammatical subject and its possessor is the experiencer. Jan 1.8/227 instead has qṭəʕlox with a personal l-agent and apparent ʕaqəl object; retain the alternation as a question.

Quarrying, brushwood cutting and honey extraction remain material extensions of I.1. Occupational qaṭoʕe remains provisionally indexed as Part act., as in round one, without claiming a productive verbal paradigm.

Round-one counts make many reader thin_cell/new_form flags obsolete: I Imperativ 1, I Infectum 1/2/3, II Infectum and II Infectum-wa already have sufficient coverage. II candle cutting is not a new form.

Finite Detransitive qṭiʕi contrasts with copular plural qṭiʕe ne. Natural breakage of makeshift supports in 4679/4683 contrasts with explicitly caused cutting of trees in 433. No extra rupture sense is needed.

Jan 2.4/777 is opaque: selection, allotment or separation is possible; the English little-goats rendering is not independent evidence. Jan 3.30/784 has an unresolved -wa/l-suffix chain and no safely recoverable referent. Neither is published as an example.
What is qṭaʕ in PrS 12/20 and 58/100: a bound adjective, a reduced Detransitive form, or a borrowing? No new Part. Pass. example is published for these uncertain shapes.

Confirm the segmentation of qṭiʕə́newa (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/59), quṭʕila (MAC Ishaq Material culture/123), qṭilux (57/148), and qoṭəḥ (PrS 20/29). Also check qṭəʕlux addressed to a woman in 59/42.
Is qṭiʕoyo/qṭiʕayto a Nomen Patiens or a lexical adjective? Does 43/52 mean ragged or isolated? Is druʕayye qṭiʕo yo in JTM 3.1/13 an agreement or transcription irregularity?
Does qṭʕ tawbe name a vow of repentance or a prescribed penance? Does the sword-subject expression in MAC Ishaq Material culture/89 conventionally express power?
What nuance distinguishes qṭʕ xabro (forget, drop, disregard), the hand-subject attachment construction, ṣabr qṭiʕ (patience or hope), and lebo qṭiʕ (fright or lost courage)?
Does qṭiʕi mi walaye (58/49) belong here or under qṭʕ 2? Retain the reader's separation analysis provisionally; do not treat it as the ordinary crossing base qaṭəʕ.

Collate the differing PrS citation systems and the 52/156 citation attached to the existing giant-head example before correcting references. Check whether the glossary's Part. Pass. and Detransitive Preterit division matches qṭiʕi/qṭiʕe in MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/13,15.
PrS 58/99 places qṭiʕ danwe before a German severing clause supplied at 58/100. Reconcile verse alignment before quoting the event.
In 102/22 who is the agent of fixing the brideprice, and how is lu goranawo related to it? The idiom does not depend on resolving the speaker transition.
Confirm qoṭaʕna (108/8) as first-person plus feminine patient contraction and qəṭʕat (108/27) with female addressee. Does 108/27 specifically mean withholding charity outside the household?
Is the heart-vein idiom in 110/16 shock, despair, or a literal physical event in this story? The figurative reading is provisional and no numbered emotion sense is added.
Confirm the l-agent/ʕaqəl alternation at Jan 1.8/227 and the preference versus confidence distinction.
Do Jan 2.5/1521 and 2.10/2458 express memory failing to reach an era, or uncertainty about an assertion? No independent memory sense has been accepted.
What is selected or separated in Jan 2.4/777, and what is the function of -le?
Parse Qṭiʕiwaylan at Jan 3.30/784: active contracted Preterit-wa or Detransitive plus holder/agent? No box example is added.
Does kiln-fire interruption mean ceasing fuel supply or extinguishing the fire? Preserve the broader reading.
Confirm ə-vocalism in Qṭəʕno at Jan 2.1/13 and the lexical status of qaṭoʕe.
Correct the conjunction dass
rationale: This is the conjunction introducing the result clause, not the article or pronoun das.

summary: A human object separated from relatives is already included in sense 1 by the existing 73/233 example; reject a duplicate social-separation sense. Instrument subjects occur in PrS 45/33; reciprocal slashing in 29/158 retains physical cutting.
Detransitive: cessation extends from blood flow to sound, breath and dawse. The last noun may denote visiting traffic rather than a period of time.

Detransitive: personal abandonment is a state corresponding to loss of contact; expanded qṭiʕoyo/qṭiʕayto is provisionally indexed as Nomen Patiens. 43/52 can instead mean ragged/destitute; its exact meaning is withheld.
Withheld charity (xer) and an allotted share (naṣib) extend the supply/payment cessation sense established in batch 1; no additional numbered meaning is needed.
Time as causer and a church community as a divisible whole extend separation already represented in round one; no duplicate social-separation sense.
Kiln fire is maintained or discontinued: i nuro is the object, not a physically severed item. Supports round-one cessation-of-process/supply sense.
Rain, continuous sound, music, schools, candle-making and seasonal produce extend round-one cessation beyond bodily flow; group the proposed practice, institutional and availability senses here.
Disappearance of lice after chemicals supports round-one local extinction, without claiming worldwide biological extinction.
Separation from books and family, and ʕalaqa as grammatical subject, support the round-one relational sense. Involuntary separation need not imply deliberate breaking of ties.
Negated mental reach in recollection contexts may belong with propositional confidence, but no separate memory sense is established.
